newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends little changed, gas lead eyed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends little changed, gas lead eyed.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures ended little changed Thursday after a quiet day of trading leading up to the Memorial Day weekend, as the market continued to consolidate after last week's rally.
Crude oil for July delivery on the New York Mercantile Exchange settled unchanged at $21.86 a barrel, after trading to a high of $22.08 from a low of $21.82.

The market believes the supply of crude oil is currently adequate, but efforts to trade crude to lower prices have been thwarted in part by nagging concerns about conflict in Iraq between Iraqi Kurds and Turkish government forces.

"There are still background concerns about these political military crosscurrents in northern Iraq. People are concerned that it could blow up into something serious," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader at Sweeney Oil in Chicago. "But right now it's probably more of a psychological force than anytrhing else," he said.
Crude oil prices are finishing a week of volatile trading that was precipitated both by last week's suprise rally and this week's expiration of the June delivery contract.

Thursday's $22.08 high, basis July, came close to Friday's high of $22.43 barrel for brief moments Thursday, posting a high of $22.08. Last Friday's high of $22.43 was the July contract's first break above $22 a barrel since February 6.
Despite efforts at profit-taking, the unrest in Turkey and uncertainty over the amount of physical demand for oil in the expired June contract has kept oil traders tentative in either direction.

Tom Bentz, analyst at High Yield Analytics in New York, believes crude oil is starting to look for direction in the unleaded gas market, as gasoline begins its peak demand season between Memorial Day and Labor Day.
"It's gasoline season. If gas is going to lead anything, this is the time," Bentz said.
Unleaded gasoline for July delivery settled at 65.10 a gallon, up 0.23 cent, while July heating oil closed at 57.85, up 0.17 cent.
